question: What is the primary way barrier methods prevent pregnancy?

options.A: Physically blocking sperm from reaching the egg
options.B: Changing the natural pH balance of the womb
options.D: Stopping the ovaries from releasing any eggs

explanation: Barrier methods act as a physical wall so sperm cannot swim up to fertilize the ovum. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why are barrier methods uniquely valuable in family planning clinics compared to pills?

options.A: They protect against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They require a doctor to insert them every time
options.C: They never fail even if used incorrectly

explanation: Condoms create a physical block against infectious body fluids, offering protection that hormonal methods cannot provide. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which barrier device is placed directly inside the vagina and features flexible rings at both ends?
explanation: The female condom is a pouch with an inner ring for placement and an outer ring that remains outside the vagina. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of these barrier devices must ALWAYS be used together with a spermicide to be effective?
explanation: Diaphragms rely on a chemical spermicide cream or jelly applied inside the dome to kill any sperm that bypasses the rim. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h2)

question: What type of lubricant should clients avoid using with latex condoms?
explanation: Oil breaks down latex material very quickly, causing the condom to tear easily during sex. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h3)

question: A client asks how long she must leave her diaphragm inside her vagina after sexual intercourse. What do you tell her?
explanation: The diaphragm must remain in place for at least six hours post-coitus to allow spermicide enough time to destroy all remaining sperm. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of barrier methods over hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: They have a zero percent failure rate
options.B: They require a surgical procedure to insert
options.C: They do not cause systemic hormonal side effects
options.D: They never need to be replaced or refitted

explanation: Because they work purely mechanically, they avoid the hormone-related side effects seen with pills or injectables. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do barrier methods generally have higher pregnancy rates in real-life use compared to implants?

options.A: They depend on the user remembering to use them every time
options.B: Body heat weakens the barrier material over months
options.C: They expire within twenty-four hours of manufacture
options.D: They dissolve completely inside the body fluids

explanation: Human error or forgetting to use a barrier during intercourse leads to higher accidental pregnancy rates. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h4)

question: How should a midwife respond to a client who fears a male condom will slip off and get lost inside her body?

options.A: Agree that it happens often and suggest surgery instead
options.B: Explain the anatomy showing the end of the vagina blocks passage
options.C: Tell her to use two condoms at the same time for safety
options.D: Advise her to stop using barrier methods immediately

explanation: Reassuring the client with clear anatomical facts helps clear up false fears and builds confidence. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an effective way to improve barrier method uptake in the community?

options.A: Hiding supplies so clients feel too ashamed to ask
options.C: Giving clear demonstrations using anatomical models
options.D: Setting up youth-friendly clinic service corners

explanation: Hiding supplies creates a barrier to access; supplies should be easily visible and accessible to encourage use. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h5)
